business_logic_plan: Business Logic Plan: Expenses document date for later period v/s posting date in previous period / qtr Data Source FBL3N.csv Required Columns: ["Company Code", "Document Number", "Posting Key", "G/L Account", "Account", "Document Date", "Posting Date", "Year/month", "Document Type", "Amount in local currency", "Local Currency", "Amount in doc. curr.", "Document currency", "Cost Center", "Profit Center", "G/L Acct Long Text", "G/L Acct Long Text.1", "Text", "Document Header Text", "Reference", "Offsett.account type", "Offsetting acct no.", "Entry Date", "User Name"] Business Requirements Q1: Which condition should trigger an exception? A1: Flag whenever Document Date month-year > Posting Date month-year (any positive lag, including across years) Q2: Should we limit the check to expense-related accounts or include all line items? A2: Include all G/L Accounts (no restriction) Q3: Do we need to exclude any typical month-end entries from the exception list? A3: No exclusions — include all document types and headers Q4: For the posting-side period, which basis should we use when comparing periods? A4: Flag only if Document Date month-year is later than BOTH the calendar month from 'Posting Date' AND the 'Year/month' period Q5: Should the exception check include both debit and credit line items, or only debits? A5: Include both debits and credits (all 'Posting Key' values) Q6: Should we apply a minimum amount threshold to flag exceptions? A6: No threshold — flag all amounts Q7: What should be the unit of reporting for exceptions? A7: One row per line item that meets the condition (line-level exceptions only) Q8: Do you want to categorize flagged exceptions by how far they cross periods? A8: No categorization — just a binary flag Q9: Do you want to limit the analysis to a specific time window? A9: No time filter — include all periods in the file Q10: Does this output structure look good to you? A10: This output structure looks perfect - proceed with this Q11: Before I generate the complete business logic plan, is there anything else I should know? A11: No, I think we've covered everything - please generate the plan Business Logic Describe the BUSINESS RULES in plain language for finance/audit users: Rule 1: Flag a line item as an exception when the accounting month-year of the Document Date is strictly later than BOTH: - the calendar month-year of the Posting Date, and - the SAP posting period shown in Year/month. This applies across months and across years. Rule 2: Interpret “later” on a month-year basis only; the day-of-month is ignored. Example: a Document Date in 2024-01 is “later” than a Posting Date in 2023-12, even if the specific days differ. Rule 3: Include all G/L Accounts without restriction. Do not limit by account range or specific G/Ls. Rule 4: Do not exclude any entries by Document Type, Document Header Text, G/L Acct Long Text, or narrative text. Accruals, provisions, reversals, and other month-end entries remain in scope. Rule 5: Include both debit and credit postings; no limitation by Posting Key or sign of amount. Rule 6: Apply no monetary threshold. Flag exceptions regardless of amount size, using the absolute value as-is for review context. Rule 7: Produce line-level exceptions only. Each output row represents a single line item that violates Rule 1. Do not include non-violating lines, even if other lines in the same document are flagged. Rule 8: No time window filter. Consider all periods available in the file. Rule 9: Provide a binary Exception_Flag to mark violations (1 = flagged, 0 = not flagged). In the delivered exception output, this will be 1 for all rows. Rule 10: Provide transparency fields to support review: - Doc_MonthYear derived from Document Date (month-year) - Posting_MonthYear derived from Posting Date (month-year) These help reviewers see the period comparison at a glance. Rule 11: Do not provide month/quarter difference metrics or categorization. The review is focused on the presence of any positive month-year lag that also exceeds the Year/month posting period. Rule 12: Clarification on dual-basis comparison: - If Document Date month-year is later than Posting Date month-year but not later than Year/month, do NOT flag. - If Document Date month-year is later than Year/month but not later than Posting Date month-year, do NOT flag. - Flag only when Document Date month-year is later than both bases simultaneously. Output Columns Company Code: Identifies the legal entity for governance and responsibility assignment. Document Number: Primary SAP reference to locate and investigate the full document trail. Posting Key: Indicates debit/credit nature of the line; useful for understanding entry direction. G/L Account: The account number for financial statement mapping and reconciliation. Account: Additional account identifier/context as present in the extract to aid matching and reporting. Document Date: The source document’s date; used to assess timing relative to posting. Posting Date: The accounting calendar date used to determine the calendar posting month-year. Year/month: The SAP posting period (YYYY/MM) used as the second basis of comparison. Document Type: Provides context on the nature of the entry (e.g., vendor invoice, journal). Amount in local currency: Primary amount for local books; used for materiality assessment during review. Local Currency: Currency code corresponding to the local amount for correct interpretation. Amount in doc. curr.: Amount as per document currency for cross-entity or cross-currency checks. Document currency: Currency code of the original document for multi-currency context. Cost Center: Operational owner/cost attribution to route follow-ups. Profit Center: Business unit responsibility for performance and control follow-up. G/L Acct Long Text: Descriptive name of the G/L for quick reviewer understanding. G/L Acct Long Text.1: Additional or alternative description where provided for clarity. Text: Line item narrative to understand business purpose. Document Header Text: Document-level narrative for additional context in investigations. Reference: External or internal reference aiding cross-document tracing. Offsett.account type: Indicates the counterparty category (e.g., vendor, customer) to guide inquiry path. Offsetting acct no.: Specific counterparty identifier to contact or reconcile against. Entry Date: When the line was entered; useful for process timing and audit trail. User Name: Originator of the posting for accountability and follow-up. Doc_MonthYear_Calculated: Month-year derived from Document Date; shows the “source” period used in the comparison. Posting_MonthYear_Calculated: Month-year derived from Posting Date; shows the calendar posting period for comparison. Exception_Flag_Calculated: Binary indicator (1 = exception) confirming the line breaches the rule that Document Date month-year is later than both the Posting Date month-year and Year/month.

# ============================================================================
# PART 1: IMPORT LIBRARIES & FILE PATH VARIABLES
# ============================================================================

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import os
import ira

fbl3n_path = "/Users/ajay/Documents/workflow_builder_v4/data/uploads/7169d4e8-b3e0-420a-a633-a6fd5eb681d5/FBL3N.csv"
output_file_path = "/Users/ajay/Documents/workflow_builder_v4/data/outputs/Expenses_document_date_for_later_period_v/s_posting_date_in_previous_period_/_qtr/output_602b2a8e-29f0-4e22-8115-b7556cf80b40.csv"

# ============================================================================
# PART 2: LOAD DATAFRAMES & IRA PREPROCESSING
# ============================================================================

# Column categories for FBL3N
DATE_COLS_FBL3N = ['Document Date', 'Posting Date', 'Year/month']
SAME_COLS_FBL3N = []
UPPER_COLS_FBL3N = []
LOWER_COLS_FBL3N = []
TITLE_COLS_FBL3N = []
NUMERIC_COLS_FBL3N = ['Amount in local currency', 'Amount in doc. curr.']

# Load FBL3N data
df_fbl3n = pd.read_csv(fbl3n_path, low_memory=False)
print(f"✓ Loaded {len(df_fbl3n):,} rows from FBL3N")

# Verify required columns
required_columns_fbl3n = [
    "Company Code", "Document Number", "Posting Key", "G/L Account", "Account",
    "Document Date", "Posting Date", "Year/month", "Document Type",
    "Amount in local currency", "Local Currency", "Amount in doc. curr.",
    "Document currency", "Cost Center", "Profit Center", "G/L Acct Long Text",
    "G/L Acct Long Text.1", "Text", "Document Header Text", "Reference",
    "Offsett.account type", "Offsetting acct no.", "Entry Date", "User Name"
]
missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns_fbl3n if col not in df_fbl3n.columns]
if missing_columns:
    raise ValueError(f"Missing columns in FBL3N: {missing_columns}")

# IRA preprocessing for FBL3N
for col in DATE_COLS_FBL3N:
    if col in df_fbl3n.columns:
        df_fbl3n[col] = ira.convert_date_column(df_fbl3n[col])

if SAME_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_strings_batch(df_fbl3n, SAME_COLS_FBL3N, rules={
        "remove_excel_artifacts": True, "normalize_whitespace": True, "case_mode": "same"})

if UPPER_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_strings_batch(df_fbl3n, UPPER_COLS_FBL3N, rules={
        "remove_excel_artifacts": True, "normalize_whitespace": True, "case_mode": "upper"})

if LOWER_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_strings_batch(df_fbl3n, LOWER_COLS_FBL3N, rules={
        "remove_excel_artifacts": True, "normalize_whitespace": True, "case_mode": "lower"})

if TITLE_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_strings_batch(df_fbl3n, TITLE_COLS_FBL3N, rules={
        "remove_excel_artifacts": True, "normalize_whitespace": True, "case_mode": "title"})

if NUMERIC_COLS_FBL3N:
    df_fbl3n = ira.clean_numeric_batch(df_fbl3n, NUMERIC_COLS_FBL3N)

print(f"✓ IRA preprocessing complete for FBL3N")

# ============================================================================
# PART 3: BUSINESS LOGIC
# ============================================================================

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create month‑year derived columns (ignoring day component)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
df_fbl3n['Doc_MonthYear_Calculated'] = df_fbl3n['Document Date'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)
df_fbl3n['Posting_MonthYear_Calculated'] = df_fbl3n['Posting Date'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)
df_fbl3n['YearMonth_Calculated'] = df_fbl3n['Year/month'].dt.to_period('M').astype(str)

print("✓ Calculated month‑year fields")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flag exceptions: Document month‑year must be later than BOTH
# Posting month‑year AND SAP Year/month period
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
condition = (
    (df_fbl3n['Doc_MonthYear_Calculated'] > df_fbl3n['Posting_MonthYear_Calculated']) &
    (df_fbl3n['Doc_MonthYear_Calculated'] > df_fbl3n['YearMonth_Calculated'])
)

df_exceptions = df_fbl3n[condition].copy()
df_exceptions['Exception_Flag_Calculated'] = 1

print(f"✓ Applied exception flag: {len(df_exceptions):,} rows flagged")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare final output with required columns + calculated fields
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
output_columns = required_columns_fbl3n + [
    'Doc_MonthYear_Calculated',
    'Posting_MonthYear_Calculated',
    'Exception_Flag_Calculated'
]

result_df = df_exceptions[output_columns].reset_index(drop=True)

print(f"✓ Final result: {len(result_df):,} rows, {len(result_df.columns)} columns")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save result
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_file_path), exist_ok=True)
result_df.to_csv(output_file_path, index=False)
print(f"✓ SUCCESS: Saved results to {output_file_path}")
